propositions: _lib_writes.py is at the 800-line hard cap enforced by CI module-size gate, blocking landing of sibling story adding two optional create_ticket arguments

The module aggregates seven independent concerns (genesis, identity/keys, status lifecycle, leaf mutations, session logs, store maintenance, signing) across 29 function definitions, each new verb or argument widening causes growth

Solution is behavior-preserving refactor splitting the file into three modules by concern: _lib_mutations.py (280 LOC, concerns 4+5+6), _lib_identity.py (231 LOC, concerns 2+7), _lib_writes.py remainder (378 LOC, concerns 1+3)

All 27 public names remain re-exported from _lib_writes with noqa comments, so __init__.py and _lib_gates.py require no changes and every rebar.<name> and rebar._lib_writes.<name> import path survives
The three new modules form a dependency-cycle-free DAG with _lib_writes importing both new modules but neither importing back, preserving one-way direction

No logic is rewritten, bodies relocate byte-identically, and all existing tests pass unmodified, validated by byte-identical proof of reconstructed pre-split blocks and name-by-name resolution assertion
